note: Re-judged 2026-11-27 independently against RFC 5216 Section 2.1.3 (rfc/full/rfc5216.txt): "The EAP Server MUST reply with an EAP-Failure packet since server authentication failure is a terminal condition." TestRFC5216ServerRepliesEAPFailureToPeerAlert and TestRFC5216ServerSendsNoEAPFailureWhenBothSidesAuthenticate only added AllowedIdentities=["eap-tls-client"] and ServerIdentity="eap-tls-server". The positive still triggers peer-side chain verification failure (asserting "verification failed" in peerErr), sends a fatal TLS alert, and requires failureAt == alertAt+1 with no EAP-Success; the negative still completes mutual auth with EAP-Success and no EAP-Failure. Verdict stands: enforced.
